chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Comparing Keppard, Bunk Johnson and Lee Collins
summary: Punch compares the rough hard attack of Keppard, Bunk's solid playing, and Lee Collins's Louis-like style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. Now, those trumpet players, let's start comparing some more of them to get that style down, if that helped you. Let's see. You see, nobody played much like Keppert, huh?

Well, Keppert was a rough fellow. He could hit them hard notes rough and quick, you know, like that. He played nice horn, but I mean, when he hit something, he just hit it hard and heavy. That's what he told me. He said, he always hit it hard. Don't blow it easy, hit it hard.
And, you know, he was a nice. Now, did Bunk play anything like him?

Well, Bunk was a nice trumpet player, but he played different from Freddie. Bunk was a good, solid, regular trumpet player, you know. That's the most man I think Buddy Petit got ideas from, Bunk. I think Buddy got right close to Bunk.
What about Lee Collins? How did he sound?

Well Lee, he's on the order of Louis. He likes Louis playing, you know, and he plays more like Louis. But he's right from here, you know, he's got the same southern style, but he's got a whole lot of Louis stuff.
